theater: 布宜諾斯艾利斯與拉普拉塔河口

battle.name: 阿根廷獨立戰爭
battle.theater: 布宜諾斯艾利斯與拉普拉塔河口
battle.brief: 1810年5月25日，布宜諾斯艾利斯市議會公開會議，第一執政委員會宣告成立，西班牙王室在拉普拉塔河口的統治由此瓦解。八年之間，克里奧羅民兵與西班牙王軍在上秘魯與安第斯山脈之間拉鋸。卡面的長槍已是舊式兵器：西班牙線列步兵1802年已廢除長槍兵，民兵方陣裡長槍與火槍仍並用。

kit.name: 長槍
kit.history: 方陣的長矛讓火槍隊站在後面。密西西比之後，長矛和火槍一起站住了。

countries: 交戰的兩方，一方是西班牙王國的拉普拉塔河總督府與依附王室的殖民地勢力，另一方是克里奧羅城鎮精英組成的革命聯盟。1810年5月之前，總督巴爾塔薩·希德戈·德·西斯內羅斯坐鎮布宜諾斯艾利斯，轄下有布宜諾斯艾利斯、庫約、塔克納、薩爾塔、聖菲、科連特斯與巴拉圭等省份及布宜諾斯艾利斯王室法庭；5月之後王權在美洲的合法性崩解，上秘魯的克魯茲王室執政會議、佩魯總督何塞·德·拉·塞爾納與查爾卡斯司法區的亞維侯爵各自宣稱代表斐迪南七世，效忠派以少數城市、要塞與銀礦為據點，常備兵力集中在內陸的駐軍點，廣大鄉間的效忠派則由鄉紳率領地方民兵作戰，忠誠的對象往往只是眼前那位總督本人。1809年的卡洛塔事變被王室當局鎮壓，效忠派以鎮壓革命為榮，士氣高昂，卻缺乏能與野戰軍正面對抗的集中兵力。革命方的核心是各省民兵與其後正規化的國民軍隊。布宜諾斯艾利斯於5月25日成立第一執政委員會，9月之後由普拉塔海峽代表會議行使省級議會權力，1816年土庫曼國會宣佈聯邦成立；北方以安第斯山脈為界分為上秘魯戰區，下秘魯的塔克納與庫斯科另立自己的執政委員會；東部海岸的何塞·赫瓦斯奧·阿蒂加斯以東岸人民的名義組織游擊隊與邊境軍，聯省議會在1790年代即已存在，1797年被西班牙當局解散，阿蒂加斯於1815年重新召集並主持。地方上，軍隊指揮官多為克里奧羅鄉紳，效忠派則以半島出生的西班牙人為主。第三方並非旁觀者。1806與1807年英國兩度派兵登陸拉普拉塔河口並攻入布宜諾斯艾利斯，迫使城市建立民兵，這段經驗直接催生了革命武裝；其後英國在美洲的擴張被革命方視為另一種外來佔領，革命派與王室派在一段時間裡都要提防海上力量。葡萄牙趁西班牙陷於歐洲戰爭出兵佔領蒙得維的亞，並在烏拉圭東岸立足，切斷革命方與阿蒂加斯的陸路聯繫。美國以武裝護航船攔截西班牙船隊，同時照常做生意。海軍方面，革命方的巡防分艦隊在查拉布魯科、拉各斯與蒙得維的亞外海周旋，決定戰局的最終仍是陸戰。
countriesEn: The two sides were, on the one hand, the Viceroyalty of the Rio de la Plata of the Spanish crown together with the colonial interests that adhered to it, and on the other the revolutionary alliance formed by the criollo elites of the towns. Before May 1810 the viceroy Baltasar Hidalgo de Cisneros governed from Buenos Aires, with the provinces of Buenos Aires, Cuyo, Tucuman, Salta, Santa Fe, Corrientes and Paraguay and the Royal Audiencia of Buenos Aires under him; after May the legitimacy of royal power in America broke down, with the Royal Junta of Cuzco in Upper Peru, Viceroy Jose de la Serna in Peru and the Audiencia of Charcas with the Marquis of Yavi each claiming to speak for Ferdinand VII. The royalists were concentrated in a few cities, fortresses and silver mines, the permanent troops being kept in the garrison towns of the interior, while across the broad countryside the royalists were local militias led by landowners, their loyalty often owed to the particular viceroy standing before them at that moment. The Cordillera rising of 1809 was put down by the royal authorities; the royalists were proud of having crushed a revolt and were in high spirits, yet they lacked the concentrated force needed to meet a field army in the open. The core of the revolutionaries was the provincial militias and, later, the national armies regularized out of them. On 25 May 1810 the First Junta was formed in Buenos Aires, and from September the Congress of the Provinces of the Rio de la Plata exercised provincial authority; in 1816 the Congress of Tucuman proclaimed the federation. In the north the theatre was divided by the Andes into an Upper Peru front, while in Lower Peru the cities of Tucuman and Cusco set up juntas of their own. On the eastern coast Jose Gervasio Artigas organised partisan bands and a frontier army in the name of the peoples of the Orient; the Congress of the East had existed in the 1790s, was dissolved by the Spanish authorities in 1797, and was reconvened and presided over by Artigas in 1815. Locally the commanders were criollo landowners almost to a man, while the royalists were led mainly by Spaniards born in the peninsula. The third parties were not bystanders. In 1806 and 1807 Britain twice landed troops at the mouth of the Rio de la Plata and marched into Buenos Aires, forcing the city to raise a militia, and that experience directly produced the armed force of the revolution; afterwards British expansion in the Americas was treated by the revolutionaries as another form of foreign occupation, and for a stretch both royalists and revolutionaries had to watch the sea. Portugal took advantage of Spain's entanglement in the European war to occupy Montevideo and to establish itself on the eastern bank of the Uruguay, cutting the land link between the revolutionaries and Artigas. American armed escorts intercepted Spanish shipping while ordinary trade went on. At sea the revolutionaries' squadron of cruisers worked off Chascomus, Lagos and Montevideo, and in the end it was the land battle that decided the war.
people: 第一個決定這場戰爭走向的人是曼努埃爾·貝爾格拉諾。1810年2月27日，他在羅薩里奧的「最佳」集會上第一次升起藍白橫條的國旗，其後被任命為北方軍團的統帥，兩度翻越安第斯山進軍上秘魯，1811年8月被迫從普拉塔河上游方向撤退，帶著殘兵穿越胡伊皮峽谷退入胡胡伊與薩爾塔；1813年2月14日在薩爾塔擊潰王室軍，卻因擅自決定進攻而遭撤換。1820年回到布宜諾斯艾利斯之後，他寫下《關於王國現狀的備忘錄》，並為後來的國歌填了詞。第二位是何塞·德·聖馬丁，他於1808年參與組織布宜諾斯艾利斯的民兵，1814年主張把重心從上秘魯轉向安第斯一線，1816年出任北方軍團統帥，1817年1月率領不到四千人的軍團越過安第斯山，在查拉布魯科與坎查拉亞達擊敗西班牙王軍，攻入聖地亞哥，1818年4月5日在邁普一役決定性地擊潰王室軍隊。他於1820年率軍北上秘魯，1824年辭軍隱居，同年去世時雙目幾乎失明。其他關鍵人物包括：推動五月暴動的國會代表胡安·何塞·卡斯特利與豪爾赫·胡安·阿蘇，主持第一執政委員會的科爾內利奧·薩阿夫德拉，1814年提出分而治之方案並在布宜諾斯艾利斯創辦報紙的馬里亞諾·莫雷諾，他後來被囚於西班牙船上押回加的斯，1821年病逝；以聯省制自居、拒絕承認布宜諾斯艾利斯中央的何塞·赫瓦斯奧·阿蒂加斯；以邊疆民兵起家、後來成為布宜諾斯艾利斯省領袖的胡安·曼努埃爾·德·羅薩斯；在智利方面率軍的貝納多·奧希金斯；以及鎮守布宜諾斯艾利斯的馬丁·羅德里格斯。對面的英國方面，1806與1807年兩次登陸的指揮官是威廉·卡爾·貝雷斯福德與約翰·惠特塞德，1807年6月29日把他們趕出首都的是利涅爾斯率領的民兵；王室軍一方的指揮官有1813年在薩爾塔戰敗的安東尼奧·何塞·薩拉維亞、1814年出任總督的霍阿金·德·拉·佩蘇埃拉、在上秘魯作戰的皮奧·特里斯唐，以及在亞維戰敗的亞維侯爵。海軍方面，美國籍的私掠船船長戴維·朱厄特在1812至1815年間為革命方奪取多艘西班牙船隻，是海上戰線最積極的名字；他的襲擊既削弱了王室的封鎖，也為革命方提供了船隻與現金。
peopleEn: The first man to shape the course of this war was Manuel Belgrano. On 27 February 1810, at the gathering known as the Optimum in Rosario, he raised the blue and white striped flag for the first time; he was then appointed commander of the Army of the North, crossed the Andes twice into Upper Peru, and in August 1811 was forced to retreat from the upper reaches of the Plata, carrying his diminished force across the Juypy ravine into Jujuy and Salta. On 14 February 1813 he destroyed the royalist army at Salta, but was removed for having ordered the offensive on his own authority. After returning to Buenos Aires in 1820 he wrote his Memoir on the Present State of the Kingdom and supplied the words of what later became the national anthem. The second was Jose de San Martin, who took part in organising the Buenos Aires militia in 1808, argued in 1814 for shifting the effort from Upper Peru to the Andes, took command of the Army of the North in 1816, and in January 1817 led fewer than four thousand men over the Andes, beating the Spanish royalists at Chacabuco and Cancha Rayada, entering Santiago, and then on 5 April 1818 crushing the royalist field army at Maipu. He led his army north into Peru in 1820, resigned his command in 1824, and died the same year, nearly blind. Among the other key figures were Juan Jose Castelli and Jorge Juan Anzu, deputies who drove the May rising; Cornelio Saavedra, who presided over the First Junta; Mariano Moreno, who proposed the plan of dividing the enemy in 1814 and founded a newspaper in Buenos Aires, was later shipped back to Spain as a prisoner and died at Cadiz in 1821; Jose Gervasio Artigas, who rested on the federal system and refused to accept the authority of Buenos Aires; Juan Manuel de Rosas, who rose from the frontier militias and later led the province of Buenos Aires; Bernardo O'Higgins, who commanded in Chile; and Martin Rodriguez, who held Buenos Aires. On the other side, the British commanders of the landings of 1806 and 1807 were William Carr Beresford and John Whitside, and the man who drove them out of the capital on 29 June 1807 was Santiago de Liniers at the head of the militia. The royalist commanders included Antonio Jose Saravia, defeated at Salta in 1813; Joaquin de la Pezuela, viceroy from 1814; Pio Tristan, who fought in Upper Peru; and the Marquis of Yavi, beaten at Yavi. At sea the most active name was David Jewett, an American privateer who took several Spanish vessels for the revolutionary cause between 1812 and 1815; his captures weakened the royalist blockade while giving the revolutionaries ships and money.
kits: 卡面的長槍是十六世紀以來歐洲步兵方陣的骨幹：一支約五至六公尺的木杆，前端裝四角形或菱形的矛頭，後端加一尺許的鐵製槍尾，配置給方陣前排的長槍兵，使後排的火槍隊可以安心射擊。西班牙軍隊在1801至1802年的整編中解散了線列步兵裡的長槍兵連，此後的正規軍一律是燧發滑膛槍加刺刀，長槍在1810年的西班牙軍中已無實戰意義；但革命之後各城按拿破崙式編制組建的民兵連隊，儀仗與街巷守備的旗手仍持長槍，密集的長槍陣也仍被視為對付騎兵衝鋒的辦法。卡面那支長槍的位置因此落在戰役的邊緣：它屬於革命軍的儀仗與民兵骨架，而不是交火時真正殺傷的兵器。真正決定交火結果的是火器。西班牙線列步兵沿用十八世紀末的.577口徑燧發滑膛槍並附刺刀，克里奧羅民兵則混用繳獲的西班牙槍、獵槍與更老舊的火槍；彈藥以紙包定裝與散裝球彈兩種供應，佩在腰帶上的彈藥盒分成十二格，便於連續射擊。騎兵用卡賓槍、軍刀與騎矛，步兵近身靠刺刀；邊疆民兵另用巨型獵刀法孔、套索與投石索，善於在沒有道路的荒原上追擊與斷糧。火砲方面，野戰砲多為四磅、六磅、八磅與十二磅的青銅前裝砲，北方軍團與安第斯軍團作戰時各攜十餘門野戰砲，重砲與攻城砲則多留在布宜諾斯艾利斯與蒙得維的亞的城防與海防工事。海上由三級戰列艦與巡防艦分擔，1806年西班牙分艦隊在巴西外海的一場風暴中折損了最大的一艘，此後在河口只剩小艇與數艘炮艦巡弋，革命方靠數艘巡防艦與私掠船維持對王室的海岸封鎖。馬匹是另一個瓶頸：克里奧羅馬體型小而耐粗飼，軍團跨山時靠上千頭騾子馱載糧秣，牛拉的卡雷塔車隊與鞍上的楚斯帕皮袋組成補給線。火藥由布宜諾斯艾利斯與門多薩的國辦藥廠供應，軍隊行軍以烤肉與馬奶酒為主食，這些細節決定了安第斯山裡的行軍速度。工事方面則用到布宜諾斯艾利斯城北的皇家堡壘、蒙得維的亞的城牆與稜堡，以及巴塔哥尼亞海岸的聖胡利安等海防據點。
kitsEn: The pike on the card was the backbone of the European infantry square from the sixteenth century onwards: a wooden shaft of some five to six metres with a four-sided or lozenge-shaped head at the front and a short iron butt-spike at the rear, carried by the pikemen of the front rank so that the musketeers behind them could fire undisturbed. In the reorganisation of 1801 and 1802 the Spanish army disbanded the pikemen companies of its line infantry, and the regular army thereafter carried nothing but flintlock muskets with bayonets, so the pike had no real combat role in the Spanish forces of 1810. After the revolution, however, the city militias were organised on Napoleonic lines, their standard-bearers still carrying pikes on parade and in street guard duty, and a dense pike line was still regarded as an answer to a cavalry charge. The position of the pike on the card therefore falls at the edge of the campaign: it belongs to the ceremonial order and the skeleton of the revolutionary militia, not to the weapons that actually killed. What decided the fighting was the firearms. Spanish line infantry still used the late eighteenth-century .577 calibre flintlock musket with bayonet, while the criollo militias mixed captured Spanish muskets with hunting guns and older muskets of other patterns; ammunition was supplied both in paper cartridges and as loose round ball, and the cartridge box worn on the belt was divided into twelve compartments so that a soldier could fire repeatedly. Cavalry used carbines, sabres and lances, infantry closed with the bayonet, and the frontier men carried the heavy facon knife, the lasso and the bolas, which served them well in tracking and cutting supply lines across country that had no roads. The artillery was mostly bronze smoothbore guns of four, six, eight and twelve pounds; the Army of the North and the Army of the Andes each took a dozen or so field pieces on campaign, while the heavy and siege guns stayed with the fortifications and coastal defences of Buenos Aires and Montevideo. At sea the work was done by third-rate ships of the line and cruisers; in 1806 the Spanish squadron lost its largest vessel in a storm off Brazil, and afterwards only boats and a handful of gun-brigs patrolled the estuary, while the revolutionaries kept up the blockade of the royalist coast with a few cruisers and privateers. Horses were another constraint: criollo horses are small and hardy, and the armies crossing the mountains relied on more than a thousand mules for carrying food and ammunition, with ox-drawn carreta wagons and the chuspa saddlebags forming the supply line. Gunpowder came from the state powder works of Buenos Aires and Mendoza, and an army on the march lived on roasted beef and mare's milk, and these details set the pace of the columns in the Andes. In the way of works the campaign used the Royal Fort north of Buenos Aires, the walls and bastions of Montevideo, and the coastal posts of Patagonia such as San Julian.
tactics: 南北兩條戰線的做法截然不同。北方戰線在1810至1811年受挫，起因是把克里奧羅的正規營連沿維拉帕拉加走廊推入上秘魯，糧道越拉越長；1811年10月，內陸山區的游擊隊與正規營連在洛羅斯井與帕拉維角互相火拼，兩個月內折損慘重。軍團主力在同年8月放棄進攻，帶著傷兵退過胡伊皮峽谷，在胡胡伊重新集結；到1813年2月，貝爾格拉諾反攻奪回薩爾塔，接著在聖洛倫索、亞維等地接連收復城鎮，北方軍團才重新取得攻勢。安第斯戰線走的是集中兵力與長距離機動的路子。1816年底，軍團在皮拉爾集結，隊伍只帶十六天口糧，分數縱隊翻越安第斯山，在查拉布魯科以側翼包抄擊潰王軍，一個月內進入聖地亞哥，隨後北進清除奇洛一帶的西班牙機關，1818年在邁普正面會戰：步兵以密集縱隊與刺刀衝鋒突破王軍右翼，騎兵在側面衝擊，後續部隊在側翼與後方包抄，戰役以近距離白刃戰收尾。殘餘的王室部隊退入蒙得維的亞，最後一批西班牙人於1818年6月登船離港。城市戰又是另一套。1806至1807年布宜諾斯艾利斯民兵以街壘、屋頂射擊與縱火街道抵抗英軍；1810年5月之後，議會廣場與港口區的群眾也成為軍事的角色，民兵在港口封鎖船隻、徵發火藥與槍械，愛國者武裝在城郊與內陸游擊。被稱為邊境戰的騎兵戰在潘帕斯與烏拉圭一帶以追擊、斷糧、包抄的游擊方式進行，1813至1814年間蒙得維的亞被圍又反圍，城市在火中數度燃燒。整體看，革命軍把主力集中在南線、以少打多取決性會戰，北方則長期陷入拉鋸，最終以省級民兵與正規營隊並存的方式運作。
tacticsEn: The two theatres, north and south, worked in quite different ways. The northern front broke down in 1810 and 1811 because criollo regular battalions were pushed up the Vilaplaga corridor into Upper Peru and the supply line stretched further and further; in October 1811 the partisan bands of the interior highlands and the regular battalions fought each other at the Well of the Loros and at the Paravi Corner, and the losses of those two months were heavy. In August of the same year the main army gave up the offensive and withdrew with its wounded across the Juypy ravine, re-forming at Jujuy; it was not until February 1813 that Belgrano counter-attacked, retook Salta and then recovered town after town at San Lorenzo and Yavi, and only then did the Army of the North regain the initiative. The Andean theatre followed the logic of concentration and long-range movement. At the end of 1816 the army assembled at Pilar with sixteen days of rations in hand, crossed the Andes in several columns, and rolled up the royalist flank at Chacabuco, entering Santiago within a month and then driving north to clear the Spanish authorities in the area of Chiloe; in 1818 the decisive engagement came at Maipu, where the infantry broke the royalist right with close-order columns and the bayonet, the cavalry charged on the flank, and the supporting columns closed in on the side and rear until the battle was settled at close quarters with the steel. The remnants of the royalist force fell back into Montevideo, and the last Spaniards to leave the city embarked in June 1818. Urban warfare followed a set of rules of its own. Between 1806 and 1807 the Buenos Aires militia resisted the British with barricades, fire from the roofs and burning streets in the quarters; after May 1810 the crowds in the Plaza de la Mayoria and the dockyards became actors in the war as well, the militia sealing ships in the port and seizing powder and muskets, while patriotic armed bands skirmished on the outskirts of the city and in the interior. The mounted war of what was called the frontier war was fought in the Pampas and in Uruguay by pursuit, cutting of supply and envelopment, and between 1813 and 1814 Montevideo was besieged and then relieved in turn, the city catching fire several times. Taken as a whole, the revolutionaries concentrated their main force in the southern theatre and won a decisive battle against odds, while the north was left grinding on for years, and the war finally ran on provincial militias and regular battalions side by side.
data: 可查證的數字大致如下。1810年5月25日，布宜諾斯艾利斯市議會召開公開會議，會後組成第一執政委員會；同日市民在街上集結，起義軍在港口取得火藥與槍械，總督府被控制。當時布宜諾斯艾利斯人口約四萬人，市區民兵約一千餘人，可用於上秘魯的遠征兵力每次不過一兩千人。第一次遠征由卡爾卡爾斯率領，約一千六百人、十二門砲；第二次由尼科馬爾基接手，擴充到三千五百人上下、十六門砲，卻在上秘魯南部受挫。1811年8月的撤退帶走約一千五百至兩千名官兵，其中傷者逾千人。薩爾塔一戰在1813年2月14日，革命軍約二千五百至三千人、十二門砲，王軍約一千五百至一千八百人、六至八門砲；王軍死傷與被俘合計數百人，被俘者約一千二百人。1814年10月6日的比爾卡普希奧，北方軍團約三千五百至四千人幾乎全軍覆沒：被俘約一千三百至一千五百人，陣亡與散失約七百至八百人，逃出者約一千四百人，十餘門砲全部淪陷。與此同時，10月26日的亞維之戰，革命軍在隆多率領下擊敗亞維侯爵的王軍，扭轉了北線的士氣。安第斯方面，1817年初的越嶺軍團規模約三千二百至三千五百人，連同輔助人員與上千頭騾子，只備十六天口糧，野戰砲十餘門。1818年4月5日邁普之戰，革命軍投入約五千至六千人，其中步兵四千上下、騎兵一千五百上下、砲約二十門；王室軍約三千六百至四千人，砲數相近。此役王軍死傷與被俘合計約一千五百至兩千人，被俘者約八百至一千人。1816年9月20日召開的普拉塔海峽代表會議有數十名代表出席，1816年7月9日土庫曼國會正式宣佈獨立，1818年6月蒙得維的亞的西班牙守軍與隨行家眷登船離開，該批船隻在數月的航程後抵達西班牙本土。
dataEn: The figures that can be given on good authority are roughly these. On 25 May 1810 the cabildo of Buenos Aires met in open session and the First Junta was formed immediately afterwards; the same day the citizens gathered in the streets, the insurgent forces took powder and muskets from the port, and the viceregal government was taken over. The city then had a population of roughly forty thousand, the urban militia numbered a little over a thousand men, and the force available for a campaign in Upper Peru was never more than one or two thousand men. The first expedition was led by Carcalas with about sixteen hundred men and twelve guns; the second, taken over by Nicomarchi, was expanded to some thirty-five hundred men and sixteen guns, and was defeated in the south of Upper Peru. The retreat of August 1811 took away between fifteen hundred and two thousand officers and men, more than a thousand of them wounded. The battle of Salta was fought on 14 February 1813, the revolutionaries numbering about twenty-five hundred to three thousand men with twelve guns against fifteen hundred to eighteen hundred royalists with six to eight guns; the royalist dead, wounded and captured together ran to several hundred, of whom about twelve hundred were prisoners. At Vilcapugio on 6 October 1814 the Army of the North, numbering some thirty-five hundred to four thousand, was practically annihilated: between thirteen hundred and fifteen hundred were taken prisoner, the killed and missing ran to some seven or eight hundred, and about fourteen hundred escaped, while a dozen guns were lost entire. At the same time, at Yavi on 26 October, the revolutionary army under Rondeau defeated the royalist force of the Marquis of Yavi and turned the mood of the northern front. On the Andean side the army that crossed the mountains in early 1817 numbered about thirty-two hundred to thirty-five hundred men, with auxiliaries and more than a thousand mules, sixteen days of rations and a dozen field guns. At Maipu on 5 April 1818 the revolutionaries committed about five to six thousand men, of whom some four thousand were infantry and some fifteen hundred cavalry, with roughly twenty guns; the royalist army numbered about thirty-six hundred to four thousand with a comparable number of guns. The royalist dead, wounded and captured together came to some fifteen hundred to two thousand, of whom eight hundred to a thousand were taken prisoner. The Congress of the Provinces of the Rio de la Plata that met on 20 September 1816 was attended by several dozen deputies; the Congress of Tucuman proclaimed independence on 9 July 1816; and in June 1818 the Spanish garrison of Montevideo and the families who accompanied it embarked, that fleet reaching Spain several months later.
cause: 戰爭的引爆點是王權的合法性危機。1808年拿破崙入侵西班牙，斐迪南七世退位後被押往法國，安達盧西亞王室的塞維亞執政會議接管了西班牙本土的權力，並著手整頓美洲殖民地的制度；新任總督西斯內羅斯於1809年抵達布宜諾斯艾利斯，而前一年卡洛塔的起事被鎮壓之後，殖民地的政治氣氛本已緊張。1810年5月，總督為處理塞維亞方面的權威問題召開公開會議，詢問市民應否接受新體制，克里奧羅派當場反對，主張由本市自行組織政府；5月20至25日之間，卡斯特利率領的民兵奪取港口的火藥庫與槍械，總督被拘，第一執政委員會於25日成立，維克托里奧在廣場的每一次講話都成為聚會的口號。更深的成因是經濟制度的不平。波旁王室的改革把十八世紀沒收的耶穌會莊園轉為國有出租的莊地與公用牧場，克里奧羅莊園主失去大片土地而政府以高價租回；波托西銀礦的開採與鑄幣受到嚴格限制，銀價下跌使總督轄區的財政與貿易同時惡化；新加的稅與關卡使本地產品難以出口，這種不滿在日後的改革主張中一再被提出。族群關係同樣緊張：半島出生的西班牙人與克里奧羅爭奪官職、貿易與土地，社會流動受限。意識形態與形勢提供了催化。美國獨立與法國革命成了克里奧羅精英的範本，報紙與愛國社團在1809年前後傳播共和觀念，青年學生與軍官開始以土生土長者自居。同時，英國1806與1807年兩度攻入布宜諾斯艾利斯，讓這座城市第一次用民兵把外軍擋在城外，市政廳在戰火中被洗劫，市議會的號召力與民兵的組織架構都被這段經歷塑造；而海上的英國與後來介入的葡萄牙也讓革命派明白，獨立不只要對付王室的常備軍，還得對付隨時可能靠岸的歐洲海軍。
causeEn: The spark was a crisis of royal legitimacy. In 1808 Napoleon invaded Spain, Ferdinand VII abdicated and was carried off to France, the Junta of Seville took over the government of the metropolitan kingdom and set about reforming the institutions of the American colonies; the new viceroy Cisneros arrived in Buenos Aires in 1809, and after the rising of 1808 in Cordillera had been put down the political atmosphere in the colonies was already tense. In May 1810 the viceroy called an open meeting to settle the question of authority on the side of Seville and asked the citizens whether they should accept the new regime; the criollo party answered in the assembly itself, holding that the city should organise its own government. Between 20 and 25 May the militia led by Castelli took the powder magazine and the muskets in the port, the viceroy was detained, and the First Junta was constituted on the 25th; every speech Victoriano delivered in the square became the rallying cry of the crowds. The deeper cause lay in the inequalities of the economic system. The Bourbon reforms turned the Jesuit estates confiscated in the eighteenth century into state-leased farms and common grazing grounds, so criollo landowners lost great tracts of land that the government then rented back to them at a high price; the working of the Potosi silver mines and the coinage of their metal were strictly restricted, and the fall in the price of silver impoverished both the finances and the trade of the viceroyalty; new taxes and customs barriers made it hard for local produce to reach outside markets, and this resentment was raised again and again in later reform proposals. Ethnic relations were tense as well: Spaniards born in the peninsula and criollos competed for offices, trade and land, and social mobility was limited. Ideology and circumstance supplied the catalyst. American independence and the French Revolution served the criollo elites as models, and newspapers and patriotic societies spread republican ideas in the years around 1809, with students and junior officers beginning to call themselves criollos. At the same time the British invasions of 1806 and 1807 taught the city to keep foreign troops out with a militia for the first time; the cabildo was sacked in the fighting, and the authority of the town council and the frame of the militia were both shaped by that experience. And the British on the sea, with the Portuguese coming after them, made the revolutionaries understand that independence meant not only defeating the royal regular army but also holding off the European navies that might land at any time.
impact: 這場戰爭直接生成了兩個國家與一段至今仍在使用的政治記憶。1816年7月9日土庫曼宣佈獨立之後，聯邦省份的名義、1810年9月20日的藍白三色旗、1812年貝爾格拉諾定下的國旗圖案與國歌歌詞，都被後來的阿根廷國家承襲下來，5月25日至今仍是國定的慶祝日之一。阿根廷這個名稱在戰爭期間由拉普拉塔河口的船運與報紙傳遍歐洲，後來成為整個國家的名稱。戰爭的代價同樣深刻。北方戰線在1810至1814年四次深入上秘魯而無功而返，軍官與骨幹大量傷亡，1811年之後北方省份的民兵不再信任正規營隊，聯省派與布宜諾斯艾利斯中央的矛盾無法調和；取而代之的是各省自治、將領自成一體的考迪羅政治，地方強人憑騎兵與邊疆民兵支配州府，國家長期陷於內戰與割據。戰爭也把邊疆推向暴力一端：潘帕斯的原住民部落長期被當作敵方與拓殖的障礙，沙漠戰役要再過半個多世紀才會展開。戰爭的經驗更直接外溢到鄰國：聖馬丁由安第斯向智利、再向秘魯推進，把獨立浪潮沿太平洋岸推上秘魯與玻利維亞的高地，玻利瓦在北方的委內瑞拉與新格拉納達戰線亦受其啟發，1826年的泛美會議與此一時期的南美邦聯構想都以此為背景。國際局勢上，英國在拉普拉塔河的門戶打開了，美國的商船隨即填補了西班牙留下的空缺，1830年代英美在河口角力與後來的砲艦外交都以此為起點；西班牙在南美洲的帝國則在1818年之後急速收縮，主力退回本土，最後一批西班牙軍人與船隻在1824年隨馬丁·羅德里格斯的遠征船隊離開秘魯，南美大陸再無西班牙常備軍。
impactEn: This war produced two countries outright and a political memory that is still in use today. After the declaration at Tucuman on 9 July 1816, the name of the federal provinces, the blue and white tricolour of 20 September 1810, the flag design and the words of the anthem settled by Belgrano in 1812, and the date of 25 May were all taken over by the Argentine state that came later, and 25 May remains one of the national holidays. The word Argentina itself travelled through the shipping and the newspapers of the Rio de la Plata during the war and spread across Europe, and later became the name of the whole country. The cost was just as deep. The northern theatre sent four expeditions into Upper Peru between 1810 and 1814 and achieved nothing; officers and veterans were killed in numbers; after 1811 the militias of the northern provinces no longer trusted the regular battalions, and the quarrel between the federalists and Buenos Aires could not be settled. What replaced it was a politics of provincial autonomy in which commanders made themselves, with local strongmen ruling the provincial capitals by means of cavalry and frontier militias, and the country remained locked in civil war and fragmentation for most of the nineteenth century. The war also drove the frontier towards open violence: the indigenous nations of the Pampas were long treated as the enemy and as an obstacle to settlement, and the campaigns into the desert would not begin for another half century or more. The experience of the war carried abroad directly: San Martin pushed from the Andes into Chile and then into Peru, lifting the wave of independence up the Pacific shore onto the highlands of Peru and Bolivia, while Bolivar's fronts in Venezuela and New Granada in the north drew their own inspiration from it, and the pan-American congress of 1826 and the projects for a league of the southern states grew out of the same background. In the wider world the door of the Rio de la Plata stood open once the British were in, and American merchant shipping promptly filled the gap left by Spain, with the Anglo-American rivalry at the river mouth in the 1830s and the gunboat diplomacy of later decades both beginning here. The Spanish empire in South America, meanwhile, contracted sharply after 1818, its main force falling back to the home country, and the last Spanish soldiers and their ships left Peru with the expedition under Martin Rodriguez in 1824, after which no Spanish regular troops remained on the continent.
result: 到1818年4月5日邁普一役，王室在拉普拉塔河地區的野戰主力被徹底消滅；同年6月，殘存守軍與西班牙家眷登船離開蒙得維的亞，總督府在本土的實際權力崩解，戰爭的陸戰部分至此結束。結果並非一帆風順：北方戰線從1810年打到1814年，四次翻越安第斯進攻上秘魯全部失敗，1811年的撤退與1814年比爾卡普希奧的損失，正是把全國兵馬耗在錯誤戰線上的帳面；莫雷諾1814年的分而治之方案意在同時在北方與南方開闢兩條戰線，結果是兩邊都無法取勝。真正決定成敗的轉折，是聖馬丁把主力集中到安第斯一線，以果斷的越嶽機動與邁普會戰取勝，再回頭收拾北方。戰爭留下的軍隊制度也影響後來。從安第斯軍團開始，革命軍第一次以正規化的步兵營、統一編制的騎兵部隊與集中的砲兵群作戰，並出現了後來阿根廷陸軍的雛形；地方民兵則在戰後成為各省的武裝力量，騎兵與邊疆民兵的傳統延續到十九世紀末，影響了內戰雙方的戰術。獨立之後的領土仍然不完整：上秘魯與玻利維亞走向獨立，阿根廷失去西北部的高地，巴西在東岸佔據大片土地，維吾利亞、科連特斯等省也陸續脫離聯邦，國家獨立的實現與國家統一的失敗同時成為下一個世紀的課題。最後，這場戰爭留下了1814年5月25日廣場的呼喊、1816年的土庫曼宣示與1817年的越嶺三個不斷被引用的起點，其後每一次的國慶與軍事紀念，都回到這三個時間點上。
resultEn: By the battle of Maipu on 5 April 1818 the royalist field army in the Rio de la Plata had been destroyed; in June of the same year the surviving garrison and the Spanish families embarked and left Montevideo, the real authority of the viceregal government in the mainland collapsed, and the land war was over. The result was not a clean sweep. On the northern front, from 1810 to 1814, four invasions across the Andes into Upper Peru ended in failure, and the retreat of 1811 and the losses at Vilcapugio in 1814 are the bill for spending the manpower of the whole country on the wrong front; Moreno's plan of 1814 to divide the enemy and fight on two fronts at once, in the north and in the south, ended with neither front able to win. The turn that really decided the outcome was San Martin's concentration of the main force on the Andean axis, the victory won by a bold crossing of the mountains and the battle of Maipu, and only afterwards the mopping up of the north. The military institutions the war left behind also shaped what came after. Beginning with the Army of the Andes, the revolutionaries for the first time fought with regularised infantry battalions, uniformly organised cavalry units and massed artillery, and the embryo of the future Argentine army appeared. The provincial militias became the armed force of the provinces after the war, and the traditions of the horseman and the frontier militia ran on into the end of the nineteenth century, influencing the tactics of both sides in the civil wars. The territory of the independent state was still not whole: Upper Peru and Bolivia went their own way, Argentina lost the highlands of the north-west, Brazil occupied large tracts on the eastern bank, and provinces such as Entre Rios and Corrientes broke away from the union in turn, so that the achievement of national independence and the failure of national unity became problems of the next century together. Finally, the war left three points that have been cited ever since, the cry in the square on 25 May 1814, the declaration at Tucuman in 1816 and the crossing of the Andes in 1817, and every later national holiday and military commemoration has returned to those three moments.
